resolutions.researcher_notes: Summit Midstream Partners, LP (SMLP) 8-K Exhibit 99.1, Q2 2020 earnings release, filed with SEC 2020-08-07: 'The estimated cost to complete the Double E Pipeline Project has decreased by approximately $50 million to $450 million as a result of locking in privately-owned rights-of-way, pipe costs and construction costs that are lower than the original budgeted amounts set at FID in June 2019.' This is a direct, exact match to the sheet's $450,000,000 SegmentCost for the Main Line. Single publisher (SMLP, the project's own 70% owner/operator) so tier=medium, independent=false -- could not find a second, distinct-publisher source stating the same $450M total-project figure. Checked and ruled out: offshore-technology.com (formerly hydrocarbons-technology.com) project profile states 'total capital investment of up to $425m' -- a DIFFERENT figure, not corroborating; PR Newswire (SMLP's own commencement-of-service release, Nov 2021) gives length/capacity/ownership but no cost figure; Pipeline & Gas Journal (Feb 2021) reports only a $175M financing-commitment figure (SMLP's remaining capital obligation, not total project cost); AOGR (Kruse, Mar 2023) discusses only the separate Red Hills Lateral extension, no Double E main-line cost; S&P Global Platts article (paywalled; read via Wayback capture 20211021154513) -- captured page is a nav/paywall shell with no article body reachable, no cost figure recoverable; naturalgasintel.com FERC-approval article (Oct 2020) gives capacity (1.35 MMDth/d) but no cost; kallanishenergy.com (financing article, Dec 2019) is unreachable -- origin returns HTTP 522 (Cloudflare origin-down) both live and via retry, and no Wayback capture exists for that URL (CDX query empty) -- this is a genuine access failure, not a deletion, so it is not cited and not marked dead. FERC Federal Register notice for the Dec 2022 Red Hills Lateral prior-notice request (fetched via federalregister.gov's raw-text API after the /unblock/ redirect blocked the HTML route) confirms Double E Pipeline, LLC as the FERC-regulated entity but states a different, smaller project's cost ($35.8 million for the 20-mile Red Hills Lateral only), not the Main Line total -- not usable for this unit. SEC EDGAR full-text search confirms this 8-K exhibit is the only SEC filing pairing 'Double E Pipeline' with '$450 million' verbatim.

Enable Midstream Partners, LP FY2014 Form 10-K (SEC EDGAR, filed 2015-02-18, CIK 0001591763), 'Interstate Transportation' section: 'EGT General. EGT is a 5,946-mile interstate pipeline that provides natural gas transportation and storage services to customers principally in the Anadarko, Arkoma and Ark-La-Tex basins in Oklahoma, Texas, Arkansas, Louisiana and Kansas. The system has the capacity to transport 6.6 Bcf/d of natural gas as of December 31, 2014.' 6.6 Bcf/d = 6,600 MMcf/d, an exact match to the sheet's 6600.00 MMcf/d. Verified live via url_verifier.py with both '6.6' and 'Perryville' present in the fetched text. Single source (one publisher, the operator's own SEC filing) -> medium/not independent per the brief's rule. Checked adjacent 10-Ks for a second, higher-confidence corroborating figure: this capacity figure moves year to year as EGT's system is expanded/contracted (FY2015-2017 10-Ks: 6.5 Bcf/d; FY2018: 6.0 Bcf/d; FY2019: 6.3 Bcf/d; FY2020: 6.2 Bcf/d) -- only the FY2014 filing states exactly 6.6 Bcf/d, so no other Enable 10-K corroborates the specific sheet value (they'd corroborate a range, not the number). The seed investor-presentation citation (Enable Midstream Q4 2017 IR Presentation PDF, on the legacy businesswire-hosted investors.enablemidstream.com subdomain) is DEAD -- the host times out/returns HTTP 409 (confirmed with a real, non-PDF error body), Wayback's availability API returns no snapshot for that exact URL, and a domain-wide Wayback CDX query for the file also came back empty (retried after an initial 'Internet Archive: Temporarily Offline' service outage resolved) -- treated as unrecoverable, not proposed. eia.gov/naturalgas/data.php and eia.gov/maps/layer_info-m.php (which now redirects live to atlas.eia.gov/search) are both generic data-portal/navigation surfaces, not deep links to a specific document, so neither is citable per the brief's rule against navigation-surface refs. CONCERN: none -- this is a data-continuity note, not a contradiction; the sheet's exact value simply dates the row to FY2014-era capacity, which is a legitimate documented figure for this system, not a competing claim.

Same Enable Midstream Partners FY2014 10-K, same passage: EGT is described as serving 'customers principally in the Anadarko, Arkoma and Ark-La-Tex basins in Oklahoma, Texas, Arkansas, Louisiana and Kansas' -- explicitly naming both Texas and Louisiana as states within the EGT system -- and the following sentence names 'Perryville, Louisiana' as the system's key off-system delivery hub where EGT interconnects with ANR, SONAT, Tennessee Gas, Texas Gas, Texas Eastern, Gulf South, Trunkline, Columbia Gas and Midcontinent Express, giving Louisiana a concrete, named anchor point consistent with the sheet's EndState/Province=Louisiana. This row represents the EGT system as a whole (a multi-state interstate network, not one point-to-point segment), so a Texas-origin / Louisiana-terminus pair is a reasonable two-point summary of a system whose western reach is the Anadarko Basin (Texas Panhandle/Oklahoma) and whose principal eastern delivery hub is Perryville, LA. Same single-source caveat as the Capacity unit -> medium/not independent. The Wayback-captured enablemidstream.com/company/operations/projects/ page (2022-12-07 snapshot; live URL times out) confirms EGT still operates across this corridor (citing the MASS and Gulf Run projects tied to EGT's Anadarko/Arkoma-to-Gulf Coast/Southeast markets) but does not name Texas or Louisiana specifically, so it was not strong enough to add as a second independent unit and was not proposed. fuelfix.com's 2013 Houston Chronicle article on the CenterPoint/OGE Enable Midstream naming (a seed citation) is now a confirmed dead link -- it 301-redirects to houstonchronicle.com/business/fuelfix/... which itself returns HTTP 404 -- and its content (a corporate-naming story) would not have supported this unit's value regardless. CONCERN: none.

The live enablemidstream.com page now 404s (domain re-pointed to a hosting platform); the Feb 2024 Wayback capture is used instead and describes the T&S segment's active systems: 'Mississippi River Transmission (MRT) serves utilities and industrial end-users in Missouri and Illinois and provides access to Mid-Continent and Northeast supply through various interconnects, including the Perryville Hub' -- present tense, current asset. Independently, Spire Inc.'s FY2024 10-K (SEC, filed 2024-11-20) states Spire Missouri purchased '28.1 billion cubic feet (Bcf) through the Enable Mississippi River Transmission LLC (MRT) system' in fiscal 2024, and that the Jan 14, 2024 peak-day demand was met with gas 'transported to St. Louis through the MRT ... transportation system' -- an unaffiliated customer confirming live, current-year throughput. Two distinct publishers (Enable/Energy Transfer and Spire) agree the pipeline is operating.

Same two sources as Status. Enable's own page lists MRT among its natural-gas transportation & storage systems; Spire's 10-K repeatedly describes gas volumes (Bcf) moved through the MRT system for its LDC. Both agree it is a natural-gas (not liquids/NGL) pipeline.

Searched hard and could not independently corroborate the specific 1,900 MMcf/d figure. Enable's own current/archived operations page states only MRT's STORAGE capacity (31.5 Bcf), not a throughput/design capacity number. CenterPoint Energy Resources Corp's 10-Ks (the pre-2013 parent, e.g. FY2011 10-K, SEC) give only combined CEGT+MRT system mileage (~8,000 miles, AR/IL/LA/MO/OK/TX) with no MRT-specific throughput figure -- and notably, the ONLY '1.9 Bcf per day' figure that appears anywhere in that 10-K belongs to a DIFFERENT CenterPoint line (CEGT's Carthage, TX-to-Perryville, LA line), which raises a CONCERN that the widely repeated '1.9 Bcf/d' MRT figure (seen on gem.wiki, uncitable) may trace back to a conflation with CEGT's capacity rather than an MRT-specific measurement -- flagging for Update review, not changing the value here. EIA's FERC Form 61-derived 'Pipeline State-to-State Capacity' dataset (EIA-StatetoStateCapacity_Jan2026.xlsx, https://www.eia.gov/naturalgas/pipelines/EIA-StatetoStateCapacity_Jan2026.xlsx) lists every MRT interstate border-crossing capacity for every year 1990-2025 under 'Enable Mississippi River Transmission, LLC' -- the single highest value across all years and all crossings is 870 MMcf/d (Illinois-St.Clair to Missouri-St.Louis, various years including 2025); no crossing ever reaches 1,900 MMcf/d. This is contrary/non-supporting evidence for the exact number, not a citable source for it, so it is not proposed as a ref, but it should inform an Update-leg review of whether 1900 MMcf/d is the correct system capacity. FERC eLibrary (the authoritative source for MRT's certificated capacity) could not be accessed -- it is a JS-rendered SPA with no server-rendered document content in this environment; the one specific document already identified as a lead (CP17-40 protest filing, elibrary.ferc.gov file_list.asp?document_id=14542921) returns only an empty Angular shell via curl/WebFetch, both with and without query-string variants. PHMSA's pipeline mileage/data pages 403'd. No WebSearch budget remained this session to pursue trade-press (S&P Global, NGI) capacity write-ups.

Enable's own T&S operations page (Feb 2024 Wayback capture) states MRT has 'approximately 1,600 miles of pipeline', which converts to ~2,574 km -- matches the sheet's 2574.00 km exactly. Pushed for a second independent source: CenterPoint's 10-Ks give only combined CEGT+MRT mileage (not MRT-specific); the EIA state-to-state capacity workbook and its 'Major Pipeline Summary' tab do not carry a mileage field, and MRT does not appear in the 'Major Pipeline Crossing Multiple State Borders' summary at all; PHMSA mileage-by-operator pages 403'd; FERC eLibrary is inaccessible (see Capacity note); no WebSearch budget remained. One CONCERN worth flagging: gem.wiki (uncitable) separately cites an older Enable investor deck (2015 Barclays presentation, itself unreadable here -- truncates at the 1MB curl limit) for '1,663 miles / 2,676 km', a slightly different figure than the current company page's ~1,600 mi/2,574 km -- reads as a rounding/measurement-vintage difference, not a conflict worth an Update flag on its own, but noting it for completeness. Filed as REFS_ADDED at medium/single-source per the rubric rather than UNRESOLVED, since the value IS supported, just not yet by two distinct publishers.

url_verifier only confirms the EIA URL is live (a 4 MB binary workbook, not substring-checkable by the tool); I opened it directly with openpyxl and confirmed the content. Its 'Pipeline State2State Capacity' tab lists, under 'Enable Mississippi River Transmission, LLC', an interstate border crossing FROM Texas (Harrison County) TO Louisiana (Caddo Parish) -- 85 MMcf/d in 2025 -- confirming the system physically originates in/touches Texas, matching the sheet's StartState/Province. The same tab lists crossings between Illinois (St. Clair County) and Missouri (St. Louis) at 715-870 MMcf/d, confirming Illinois as the system's northern terminus, matching EndState/Province. Independently, CenterPoint Energy Resources Corp's FY2011 10-K (SEC, the pre-2013 parent/operator) describes 'CenterPoint Energy-Mississippi River Transmission, LLC (MRT) is an interstate pipeline that provides natural gas transportation, natural gas storage and pipeline services to customers principally in Arkansas, Illinois and Missouri' -- an independent, government-filed corroboration of the Illinois endpoint. Two distinct, independent sources (EIA/FERC Form 61 data and a SEC 10-K) agree on the Texas-to-Illinois span.

Energy Transfer Partners' FY2009 Form 10-K (SEC EDGAR, filed 2010-02-24) lists 'East Texas Pipeline' as one of its active operating intrastate transportation pipelines. The company's own website (Wayback capture of energytransfer.com/ops_intrastate.aspx, June 2017) independently re-confirms it as a currently operating asset years later ('Our intrastate transportation and storage segment... our East Texas pipeline'). Both documents are self-published by the same company (Energy Transfer / its predecessor ETP), so this is ONE origin -- marking independent=false and tier medium rather than high. The original seed bit.ly link (bit.ly/2lWcvjz) now resolves to Energy Transfer's current generic homepage, so I traced the intended intrastate-ops page via Wayback captures instead.

Both the FY2009 10-K and the 2017 company website describe the East Texas Pipeline as part of Energy Transfer's 'natural gas transportation pipelines' intrastate segment. Same origin (Energy Transfer) in both documents, so independent=false, tier medium.

CONCERN: could not confirm a clean 2008 in-service/start year, and found evidence the pipeline is older. Energy Transfer Partners' 2008 SEC prospectus supplement (424B2, filed 2008-07-16, SEC EDGAR accession 0000950129-08-003976) already describes the East Texas pipeline as an existing asset with ~700 MMcf/d of capacity in mid-2008, and describes a then-pending 'Katy expansion' (56 miles of 36-inch pipe) that would raise its capacity 'from approximately 700 MMcf/d to more than 1.1 Bcf/d,' originally expected in service Q4 2008. The FY2009 10-K's project-completion table (SEC EDGAR accession 0001193125-10-039066) shows the Katy expansion's actual completion was February 2009, not 2008. So the pipeline predates 2008 (at lower capacity), and the specific expansion phase that pushed it toward its later, larger footprint completed in early 2009. No source found pinning a 2008 in-service date for the segment as GEM records it. Declining to cite a ref for StartYear1=2008; flagging the pre-2008 origin + Jan/Feb-2009 expansion-completion evidence for Update to reconcile.

FY2009 10-K, under 'East Texas Pipeline': 'Capacity of 2.4 Bcf/d' -- exact match to the sheet's 2400.00 MMcf/d. The 2017 company website snapshot independently repeats the identical figure ('East Texas Pipeline: Capacity of 2.4 Bcf/d') years later, confirming stability of the value over time. Same origin (Energy Transfer) both times, so independent=false, tier medium.

FY2009 10-K: 'The East Texas pipeline is a 370-mile natural gas pipeline.' 370 miles = 595.5 km, matching the sheet's 595.00 km (LengthKnownUnits=km) almost exactly. The 2017 website snapshot independently repeats 'Approximately 370 miles of natural gas pipeline.' Same origin both times, independent=false, tier medium.

FY2009 10-K and the 2017 website both describe the East Texas Pipeline as connecting treating facilities to Energy Transfer's Southeast Texas System and 'serv[ing] producers in East and North Central Texas' with access to the Katy Hub -- consistent with both StartState/Province and EndState/Province recorded as Texas, United States on the sheet (no more specific start/end city is given in either GEM row or these sources). Same origin, independent=false, tier medium.

Kinder Morgan's own current Natural-Gas operations index page (live, fetched directly): 'El Paso Natural Gas (EPNG) is a 10,140-mile pipeline system which transports natural gas from the Rockies, San Juan, Permian and Anadarko basins to Colorado, California, Arizona, Nevada, New Mexico, Oklahoma, Texas, and Northern Mexico' -- present-tense description of a currently active system, listed among KM's in-service pipeline assets. Wikipedia (live, fetched directly, en.wikipedia.org/wiki/El_Paso_Natural_Gas): 'El Paso Natural Gas (EPNG) is an American company and a 10,140-mile pipeline system consisting of a system of natural gas pipelines that brings gas from the Permian Basin in Texas and the San Juan Basin in New Mexico and Colorado to West Texas, New Mexico, Nevada, California, and Arizona' -- also present tense, no cessation/retirement mentioned, article's infobox lists no end date. Two distinct publishers (Kinder Morgan, Wikipedia) both describe EPNG as a presently operating pipeline system -> supports 'operating', high/independent. Neither source uses the literal word 'operating', so this is a present-tense/no-retirement-mentioned inference rather than an explicit status statement -- consistent with how this cohort treats company-overview pages per the brief's calibration.

Kinder Morgan's page (live): 'El Paso Natural Gas (EPNG) is a 10,140-mile pipeline system which transports natural gas...'. Wikipedia (live): 'Type Natural Gas Pipeline / Industry Pipeline' infobox fields, and body text 'a system of natural gas pipelines that brings gas from the Permian Basin...'. Both distinct publishers explicitly identify this as a natural-gas pipeline -> matches sheet's Fuel='Gas', high/independent.

Searched hard, found no source giving 1997 as an in-service/start year for EPNG. Checked: (1) Wikipedia's full History section (fetched directly) -- covers the original mainline completion (Texas-California pipeline completed to Los Angeles, Dec. 1947, cited to American Gas Journal), the 1954-1996 Blue Flame Building headquarters period, Tennessee Gas Pipeline's acquisition BY EPNG's later parent in 1996, and Ruby Pipeline's 2010 creation -- no 1997 event appears anywhere in the article. (2) Kinder Morgan's own current Natural-Gas overview page -- no history/date content at all, present-tense description only. (3) Kinder Morgan's 2018 Form 10-K (SEC EDGAR, fetched directly) -- the only '1997' hit in the entire document is an unrelated line about the auditing firm ('We have served as the Company's auditor since 1997'), not a pipeline in-service date. (4) The seed FERC pipeline-code-list and EIA pipeline-projects-table citations are indexes, not dated history sources, and were not accessible in a form that would date EPNG's own in-service year specifically (EPNG's mainline long predates any FERC Form 549B code list or EIA project-tracking window). EPNG's mainline in-service year is documented elsewhere as 1947 (Wikipedia/Texas State Historical Association), which conflicts with the sheet's 1997 rather than supporting it -- but per the no-value-change rule this is not asserted as a correction, since '1997' could plausibly key off a specific expansion, FERC certificate, or corporate-restructuring event not yet located, and one online source search is not exhaustive for a specific historical fact this granular. Recommend a targeted FERC eLibrary docket search (not accessible from this environment) as the next step if this unit is revisited.

Kinder Morgan's 2018 Form 10-K (SEC EDGAR, fetched directly with a compliant SEC User-Agent; full text searched), Natural Gas Pipelines segment asset table, as of Dec. 31, 2018: the combined 'EPNG/Mojave' pipeline system entry lists Design Capacity of 5.65 Bcf/d (=5,650 MMcf/d) and 10,660 combined miles, serving 'Northern New Mexico, Texas, Oklahoma, to California' and connecting to the 'San Juan, Permian and Anadarko basins.' This is within ~1% of the sheet's 5,600.00 MMcf/d and is the only capacity figure located for the EPNG system (the combined EPNG/Mojave figure vs. the sheet's EPNG-only figure, and Mojave's separate ~500-mile length per Kinder Morgan's own materials, is consistent with the ~520-mile length gap between the 10-K's 10,660 mi and the sheet's 10,140 mi EPNG-only). Only ONE distinct publisher located for this specific figure (Kinder Morgan, via its own SEC filing) -- Wikipedia and the KM overview page both omit any capacity number, and EIA's Major Pipeline Summary dataset (State-to-State Capacity, Jan 2023 vintage, checked directly) tracks 'El Paso Nat Gas Co' only at the segment level (e.g., Arizona-California segment M3: 4,504 MMcf/d in 2022), which is a different granularity and does not independently corroborate a single system-wide 5,600 MMcf/d figure. Per the brief's tier rule, one source => medium, independent: false.

Kinder Morgan's page (live, fetched directly): 'El Paso Natural Gas (EPNG) is a 10,140-mile pipeline system...' -- exact match to the sheet's 10,140.00 mi. Wikipedia (live, fetched directly): 'El Paso Natural Gas (EPNG) is an American company and a 10,140-mile pipeline system...' -- identical figure, independently written/maintained article. Two distinct publishers (Kinder Morgan and Wikipedia) agree exactly on 10,140 miles -> high/independent. (Kinder Morgan's 2018 10-K gives a combined EPNG/Mojave figure of 10,660 miles, consistent with EPNG-alone at 10,140 mi plus Mojave's separate mileage, but not used as one of the two corroborating sources here since it is the same publisher as the KM website.)

KM's 2018 10-K asset table gives the same EPNG/Mojave supply-region description including 'San Juan, Permian and Anadarko basins' verbatim -- but this and the KM website are the SAME publisher (Kinder Morgan), so together they count as one origin. Wikipedia (live) gives a related but not identical description: 'brings gas from the Permian Basin in Texas and the San Juan Basin in New Mexico and Colorado' -- names two of the sheet's three basins (Permian, San Juan) but does NOT mention Anadarko, and is a different publisher. Because the second publisher only partially agrees (2 of 3 basins, omitting Anadarko), this does not meet the bar for a full 'high' corroboration -- kept at medium/independent:false, with Kinder Morgan (website + 10-K, one origin) as the source that fully matches the sheet's exact three-basin value, and Wikipedia noted in-text as partial corroboration rather than counted as the second agreeing source.

Kinder Morgan's page (live): EPNG 'transports natural gas from the Rockies, San Juan, Permian and Anadarko basins to Colorado, California, Arizona, Nevada, New Mexico, Oklahoma, Texas, and Northern Mexico' -- names both Texas and California among the states served/connected. Wikipedia (live): the system 'brings gas from the Permian Basin in Texas... to West Texas, New Mexico, Nevada, California, and Arizona' and its infobox 'Area served' lists 'California, Arizona, Nevada, New Mexico, Oklahoma, Texas, and Northern Mexico' -- also confirms both Texas and California as part of the pipeline system's footprint, and the original mainline history (cited in Wikipedia to a 1947 American Gas Journal article, 'Texas-California Pipeline Completed To Los Angeles') independently supports a Texas-to-California trunk. Two distinct publishers (Kinder Morgan, Wikipedia) corroborate the sheet's StartState/Province=Texas and EndState/Province=California -> high/independent. Note: neither source is granular enough to confirm the specific unnamed StartLocation/EndLocation city fields, only the state-level values.

Searched hard, no independent source confirms 1998 as this system-level row's start year. gem.wiki's own citation for 'Start year: 1998' traces SOLELY to the banned bit.ly/2smVBv2 -> abarrelfull.wikidot.com (confirmed by resolving the shortener with curl -sI), so it is not usable even as a lead beyond the number itself. Checked: (1) Wikipedia's Florida_Gas_Transmission article -- no start year given at all. (2) EIA's official 'Historical Projects (1996-2024)' pipeline-projects table (full scan of all ~20 Florida Gas Trans Co rows 1996-2024) -- the only 1998 entry is the small 'FGT Alabama Power Lateral' (Docket CP98-249, +62 MMcf/d, 1 mile, AL only), a minor lateral addition, not a system-wide in-service/founding date. (3) Kinder Morgan's FGT asset page (live 404; Wayback capture used) and Rextag's FGT informational posting -- neither states an in-service year. (4) Kinder Morgan's FY2018 10-K (SEC EDGAR) -- describes FGT only as a present-day '5,300-mile' system, no history/founding date. (5) SEC EDGAR full-text search for 'Florida Gas' + '1959' (488 hits) and spot-checked the most promising non-fund hit (Florida Public Utilities Co 10-K/10-Q) -- describes FPU's FGT transportation contracts from 1990-1992 onward, no founding-year statement for FGT itself, so this neither confirms nor contradicts 1998. (6) Web search engines other than WebSearch (DuckDuckGo html/lite, Bing, Ecosia, Mojeek) were tried via curl as a WebSearch-budget-exhaustion workaround and all returned bot-check shells or empty result sets, not usable. No CONCERN is filed -- there is no affirmative evidence 1998 is wrong (FGT's original mainline dates to 1959 per general industry knowledge, but I could not independently source that either, so I am not asserting a contradiction on an unsourced recollection).

Searched hard, no independent source confirms 1059.44 MMcf/d. gem.wiki itself states this figure as '1059.44 million cubic feet per day / 3 billion [sic] cubic meters per day' and cites it SOLELY to the banned abarrelfull URL. Cross-check: 1059.44 MMcf/d converts, essentially exactly, from 30,000,000 cubic metres/day (30,000,000 x 35.3147 ft3/m3 / 1e6 = 1059.44), i.e. this looks like a metric-origin figure (probably '30 mcm/d') converted once and never independently re-verified since -- consistent with it never having been re-sourced beyond the original abarrelfull entry. Checked for a real modern figure instead: Rextag's FGT informational-posting page states current whole-system capacity as 3.7 Bcf/d (i.e. ~3,700 MMcf/d), and Kinder Morgan's FY2018 10-K gives the system as '5,300 miles' with no capacity figure -- neither corroborates 1059.44, and the Rextag figure is more than 3x higher, consistent with 1059.44 being a stale/historical design-capacity snapshot from well before the Phase IV-VIII expansions (EIA's Historical Projects table shows +200/+298/+180/+130/+121/+820/+343 MMcf/d added in phases from 2001-2011 alone). EIA's own 'Pipeline State2State Capacity' dataset (Jan-2021 vintage, full history 1990-2020 for every Florida-Gas-Trans-Co state-pair segment) was checked in full: none of its per-segment capacity values (e.g. Escambia AL->Santa Rosa FL: 1475 in 1998, 2224 by 2003+) is 1059.44 or a component that sums/matches it exactly, and none carry two-decimal precision (all are whole MMcf/d). No independent source with this specific number was found. No CONCERN filed -- not asserting the number is wrong, only that it is unconfirmed outside the banned source.

Two distinct publishers independently corroborate the STATE-level portion of this Location group (StartState/Province=Texas, EndState/Province=Florida, both StartCountryOrArea/EndCountryOrArea=United States): Wikipedia's Florida Gas Transmission article states the pipeline 'brings gas from Texas, Louisiana, Mississippi, and Alabama into Florida.' Kinder Morgan's own FGT asset page (live URL now 404s -- confirmed via curl -o -w '%{http_code}' -- so the Wayback capture from 2020-04-13 is cited instead) independently states FGT 'transports natural gas from south Texas to south Florida.' CAVEAT (not a CONCERN, a precision note): neither source, nor any other source checked (Rextag informational posting, Kinder Morgan's FY2018 10-K via SEC EDGAR, EIA's pipeline-projects/state2state-capacity tables), names the exact towns 'Port Lavaca' or 'Miami' as the specific origin/terminus points -- those two town-level names (this unit's StartLocation/EndLocation primary values) remain independently unconfirmed at that granularity, even though gem.wiki's own citation for them (fgttransfer.energytransfer.com/ipost/FGT/maps/system-map) was checked directly and found to be a login-gated portal with only a generic interconnect-map list, no town-level endpoint labels -- so it would not have supported the exact claim either. Port Lavaca (Calhoun County, TX) is geographically consistent with FGT's known South Texas receipt corridor near Matagorda/Wharton counties (see the East-West Project sourcing on P4051, same system), and Miami-area delivery is consistent with FGT's documented major customer Florida Power & Light (Wikipedia) and its Turkey Point Lateral project (EIA Historical Projects table, 2006, FL) -- but these are inferences from adjacent facts, not direct naming, so they are not cited as independent confirmation of the exact town-level values.

FERC's own Notice of Availability of the Draft Environmental Impact Statement for the Gulf Crossing Project (Federal Register, publisher: Federal Energy Regulatory Commission, Docket Nos. CP07-398-001/CP07-401-000) states the project consists of 'Approximately 353.2 miles of 42-inch-diameter natural gas transmission pipeline extending east-southeast from Grayson County, Texas and Bryan County, Oklahoma to Madison Parish, Louisiana' -- an exact match (353.2 rounds to the sheet's 353.00 mi). This is a single publisher, so tier is medium/independent false rather than high. For context (not proposed as refs, since they describe a materially different figure/stage and would not tightly support the exact 353.00 value): Boardwalk Pipeline Partners' own SEC 10-Ks describe a slightly larger as-designed/as-built mileage for the same pipeline -- 355 mi (FY2006, initial project announcement), 357 mi (FY2007 and FY2008/2009, as constructed) -- and Gulf Crossing's own company website (Wayback capture of gulfcrossing.com/AboutUsGC.aspx, 2019) and Boardwalk's FY2018 10-K both later describe the system as approximately 375 miles. Read together these look like normal growth from the original 2007 FERC-filed mainline mileage (353.2 mi, matching the sheet) to a later as-built figure inclusive of loops/laterals added after the FERC EIS (356.3 mi mainline + 17.8 mi loop per FERC's March 2008 Final EIS notice, E8-6315) to an even later 'system' total (357-375 mi) as compression/looping was added over the 2009-2019 period. None of this contradicts the sheet's 353.00 mi as the originally-proposed/certificated mainline length; it just means later company disclosures describe the grown system rather than the original filed mileage, so I did not force them in as a second independent source for the SAME 353.00 figure. [QC] relevance unrecorded (no name_found on any verification).

resolutions.researcher_notes: Boardwalk Pipeline Partners' FY2008 Form 10-K (SEC EDGAR, filed 2009-02; automated substring screen failed on my literal search label but I fetched and grepped the document directly and confirmed the exact sentence) states: 'Gulf Crossing's supply sources are mainly unconventional gas sources in the Barnett Shale and Caney Woodford Shale' -- an exact match to the sheet's 'Barnett Shale, Texas; Caney/Woodford Shale, Oklahoma.' The Wayback capture of Gulf Crossing's own company page (gulfcrossing.com/AboutUsGC.aspx, 2019-07-26 snapshot) independently repeats: Gulf Crossing 'provides takeaway capacity from the Barnett Shale in Texas and the Caney/Woodford Shale in Oklahoma.' Enterprise Products Partners L.P.'s own asset table (both on its investor-relations 'Natural Gas Pipelines & Services' page, Wayback 2022-09-25 snapshot -- the live URL now 404s -- AND its FY2023 Form 10-K filed with the SEC, 2024-02-28, CIK 0001061219) name 'Texas Intrastate System' by its exact GEM name and list 'Enterprise' / Enterprise Products Partners as Operator. The IR page states: 'The remainder of our Texas Intrastate System is wholly owned' (after carving out a leased portion of the Wilson storage facility). The 10-K's asset table lists the Texas Intrastate System's Ownership Interest as 'Various' with footnote (5): 'We proportionately consolidate our undivided interests, which range from 22% to 80%, in 1,469 miles of the Texas Intrastate System' -- out of the system's total 6,719 miles, meaning roughly 5,250 miles (~78%) is wholly (100%) owned by Enterprise and the remaining ~1,469 miles is a partial/undivided joint interest at 22-80% depending on the segment. Both documents are Enterprise's own statements (one publisher, different venues) -> medium/not independent, not high. Treated as REFS_ADDED (not a full match) because the value is directionally and substantially correct -- Enterprise IS the sole operator and the clear majority owner -- but the sheet's blanket 'Owner1% = 100.00%' is a simplification of a more nuanced structure with a real minority undivided-interest carve-out. CONCERN: the Texas Intrastate System is NOT uniformly 100% Enterprise-owned end to end -- per Enterprise's own FY2023 10-K footnote (5), about 1,469 of its 6,719 miles are proportionately-consolidated undivided interests ranging 22%-80% (i.e., partially owned with unnamed co-owners), while the remaining ~5,250 miles are wholly owned. This does not contradict Enterprise being the correct Owner1/operator of record, and no source names a specific second owner entity to add as Owner2, so no value change is proposed -- flagging for awareness only, since a future editor with access to the segment-level breakdown may want to split this network-level row's ownership more precisely.
